[[Deep North]] |Snow-capped hills and forests with frozen rivers, inhabited by [[Moose]], [[Elaking]], and [[Gammeltroll|Gammeltrolls]]. |Northern edge of the world |} == Alternative biomes == Each biome patch has a chance to have modifiers applied to it on world generation, but only a certain distance from the world center. These modifiers can have the following effects: * Affect foliage, like more [[Raspberries]] or only [[Birch]]es in the Meadows, or only stubs in the Black Forest * Generate additional structures, like [[Large Bone]]s in the Swamps, Plains or Mistlands, or more [[Tar Pit]]s in the Plains * Increase the chance for [[creature level|starred]] creatures * Enable the spawning of certain creatures not normally encountered in the biome, such as [[Bat]]s in the Swamp, or increase existing chances for a creature to spawn, like more [[Abomination]]s * Disable the spawning of creatures native to the biome Several modifiers can affect a single area at once. The following biomes can be affected: * [[Meadows#Alternative biomes|Meadows]] has 8 modifiers. * [[Black Forest#Alternative biomes|Black Forests]] have 8 modifiers. * [[Swamp#Alternative biomes|Swamps]] have 5 modifiers. * [[Mountain#Alternative biomes|Mountains]] have 3 modifiers. * [[Plains#Alternative biomes|Plains]] have 5 modifiers. * [[Mistlands#Alternative biomes|Mistlands]] have 6 modifiers. Oceans, the Ashlands and the Deep North do not have any alternative variants. ==Trivia== *The term "biome" comes from the [[wikipedia:biome|ecological concept of the same name]]. *At ''Valheim's'' early access launch in February 2021, five of the planned nine biomes were made available to explore. The other four were accessible, but lacked any meaningful content. ** As of the full release in September 2026, all biomes excluding the Ocean are fully implemented. An Ocean overhaul was ultimately abandoned, with the argument that it only serves the role of a highway between other biomes, which do have meaningful content. * Alternative biomes were introduced in the [[1.0]] release. {{Biomes}} [[de:Biom]] [[ru:Биомы]] [[pt-br:Biomas]] [[uk:Біоми]] [[cs:Biomy]] [[zh-tw:生物群落]] [[Category:Biomes| ]]

[[File:Greyling 0S.png|thumb|A [[greyling]], an aggressive creature found in the [[Meadows]].]] '''Creatures''' are non-player characters which are found throughout ''[[Valheim (world)|Valheim]]''. They can be split to four categories: * [[Creatures#Bosses|Bosses]] are powerful aggressive creatures that must be summoned. Killing them unlocks [[Forsaken power|Forsaken powers]], increases [[Global Keys|world difficulty]] and provides loot to progress in the game. * [[Creatures#Minibosses|Minibosses]] are unique, named, aggressive creatures that you can find in specific dungeons. Killing any given miniboss will reward with one of [[Hildir's Chests]]. * [[Creatures#Aggressive creatures|Aggressive creatures]] will attack players when alerted. They also drop loot when killed. * [[Creatures#Passive creatures|Passive creatures]] provide resources when killed (or harvested). They will never attack players. * [[Creatures#NPCs|NPCs]] are friendly creatures/characters that cannot be killed and may provide some service or help to the player. == Bosses == Bosses, also known as the '''Forsaken''', can be summoned by offering specific items (hinted by the [[Runestone#Altar Runestones|Runestones]]) at their specific spawn site. They have increased HP and special attacks compared to regular creatures. A boss site is automatically marked on the player's map by reading the runestone in the specific biomes. There are multiple spawn locations for every boss. One-star creatures have double the health and deal 150% damage, while two-stars have triple the health and deal double damage. '''Behavior''' *Creatures will give up chasing after unable to attack for 60 seconds or unable to detect the target for 30 seconds. *Some creatures have a max chase range. After chasing that far they will give up if unable to detect the target for 1 seconds. *After unable to attack for 15 seconds, creatures will focus structures for 15 seconds if they can't reach the target. *Creatures only attack walls and doors if they aren't able to reach the target player. *Some creatures are afraid of fire and will flee from it. *Some creatures try to avoid fire and will be passive near it. *Some creatures circulate around the target while waiting to attack. *Swimming creatures try to flee towards water if forced on ground. *Creatures passively regenerate 1.67% of their max health every minute (100% over 60 minutes). *Creatures gain +30% more effective health per each additional player within 100 meters. E.g. 3 players = +60% effective health. **This is updated whenever the creature takes damage. *Creatures gain +4% more damage per each additional player within 100 meters. '''Copper Ore''' can be refined into [[Copper]] in a [[Smelter]].

Two Copper can be further processed at a [[Forge]] with [[Tin]] to yield [[Bronze]].

== Availability ==
It can be mined from [[Copper Deposit]]s which can be found in [[Black Forest]] [[biomes]] using any [[Pickaxes (skill)|Pickaxe]]. Such deposits have subtle bronze-colored streaks that reflect the sunlight. It is the only visual feature that distinguishes them from typical stone boulders.

Copper deposits are generated in a large size which extends down into the ground, so digging deep underneath the surface is necessary to fully extract a single deposit.

== Notes ==
* A way of farming Copper is to dig the earth all around the deposit until it crumbles on itself into Copper Ores. 
* Like other metals, Copper Ore cannot be teleported without a [[Portal stone]].
* The attacks of a [[Troll]], despite being harmless to normal terrain, cause immense damage to Copper Ore. If the player has no pickaxe or simply yearns for a change from their usual monotonous mining method, a Troll can make for a great alternative.

The '''Deep North''' is a vast, snowy [[Biomes|biome]], found in the northernmost part of ''Valheim''. Described as a "postcard of a Christmas landscape", it contrasts the hordes of the fiery [[Ashlands]] with fewer but stronger creatures.

Akin to the Ashlands, the Deep North landmass is separated from other biomes by an [[Ocean]] and borders the [[World Edge]] on the northern side. There is no equivalent of the boiling sea preventing access to the biome, however, defeating [[Fader]] is still required to progress through the biome, and strong enemies pose a threat. Sheets of ice float along the shores, a potential danger to any ship attempting to dock here.

As in the Mountains, all weather in the Deep North is freezing, day and night, so players without frost resistant clothes or [[Frost Resistance Mead]] in effect take continuous [[Freezing Effect|freezing]] damage outdoors. See [[#Weather|Weather]] below.

The biome was the focus of the [[Version history|1.0 update]].

Wind intensity is capped at 1. A blizzard's wind range lies above that cap, so the wind always blows at full strength during a blizzard.

A player outdoors and away from a fire gets the [[Freezing Effect|Freezing]] effect: no health regeneration, 60% slower stamina and eitr regeneration, and one point of damage every second. Near a fire or in shelter, the player gets the [[Cold Effect|Cold]] effect instead (50% slower health regeneration, 25% slower stamina and eitr regeneration), and a fire in shelter removes both. Slight, normal or very high frost resistance prevents both effects.

While it snows, snow builds up on structures that have no roof above them and are not inside a [[Shield Generator]]'s shield. It can be cleared with the [[Snow Shovel]].

The '''Blast Furnace''' is a structure used to process advanced raw metals into ingots. Although it performs a similar function to the [[Smelter]], it cannot smelt the ores that the Smelter can.

== Building ==
It is unlocked after the player has killed [[Moder]] and built an [[Artisan Table]].

Blast Furnaces can be placed directly onto terrain and stone structures. Currently, they cannot be placed on wood structures, but it is possible to bypass this to an extent by terraforming terrain with a [[Hoe]] to be in line with wooden floors.

Unlike the Smelter, Blast Furnaces have both of their refueling ports to the left of the bar chute.

== Usage ==
The Blast Furnace is used to process certain raw materials into [[metal]] using {{Item link|Coal}} as fuel. Materials that can be smelted are:

The '''Sap Extractor''' is a structure used to harvest {{Item link|Sap}} from [[Ancient Roots]] in the [[Mistlands]] [[Biomes|biome]].

==Building==
Sap Extractors can be built on Ancient Roots within the range of a [[Workbench]].

It requires [[Black Metal]], [[Yggdrasil Wood]] and a [[Dvergr Extractor]], obtained from [[Dvergr Component Crate]]s.

==Usage==
When placed on [[Ancient Roots]], the Sap Extractor will extract {{Item link|Sap|1}} from the root every 60 seconds. It can hold a maximum of 10 Sap and glows green if it contains any Sap to harvest. As it is extracting, green particles will leave the top and bottom of the extractor. The particles will stop appearing at the top once the extractor is full, or if attempting to extract from a completely dried root.

As Ancient Roots regenerate Sap much slower than it is extracted, at 1 sap per {{duration|400}} (see their page for details). It is strategic to relocate extractors between multiple roots. Destroying or deconstructing an extractor with Sap inside does not drop the Sap.

==Tips==
* The required Black Metal cannot easily be teleported to the extraction site:
** Therefore, it is advisable to transport some by [[Boat]] before setting off to explore the Mistlands. Ideally, scout the biome for a location with many Ancient Roots as well as tillable ground in proximity, and if so, carry over the Black Metal and set up an outpost.
** Alternatively, the Mistlands biome are generally close to the [[Plains]], so it is possible to acquire [[Black Metal Scrap]] on site. The [[Iron]] needed to build a [[Blast Furnace]] can be mined from [[Ancient Sword]] or [[Ancient Armor]]. All other materials can be teleported via [[Portal]].

'''Ancient Roots''' are a resource found in the [[Mistlands]] biome. [[Sap Extractor]]s can be placed on them to harvest [[Sap]].

==Availability==
Ancient Roots can be commonly found in Mistlands, at ground level. They emit a green light glow which can be seen through the mist.

== Sap harvesting==
Each root dries up as [[Sap]] is extracted from it using a [[Sap Extractor]]. Each Sap Extractor collects and stores one sap every 60 seconds. Multiple sap extractors can be placed on one Ancient Root.

The reservoir of sap in an ancient root regenerates at a rate of 1 sap per {{duration|400}}, up to a maximum storage of 50 sap (obtained in {{duration|20000}}). Thus, sap is a renewable resource. 

Ancient Roots have three visual states: Full, half dried, and dried up.

The attack does high damage to [[Grausten Structures|grausten]] and weaker structures, similar to a Lox, and it can even damage [[Factions|allied creatures]]. == Aftermath == Defeating Asksvin allows the player to loot the following items. === Drops === {{Drop table|{{drop row|item=Asksvin trophy|0star=10%|1star=10%| 2star=10%}} {{drop row|item=Asksvin bladder| 0star=1|1star=2| 2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Asksvin hide| 0star=2|1star=4| 2star=8}} {{drop row|item=Asksvin tail| 0star=2|1star=4| 2star=8}}}} Parts for a buildable [[Asksvin Skeleton]] can also be found separately in the [[Ashlands]], but they drop from destroying Asksvin Skeletons already there, not from killing Asksvin. == Taming == ''For general taming information and strategies, see [[Taming]].'' Similar to the [[Wolf]], Level 3 (two-star) Asksvin only spawn at night. Like any creatures spawned at night, Level 3 Asksvin will attempt to flee the active area and despawn during daytime hours if the taming process has not begun. This can be prevented by either (A) trapping them in a pit or pen that they cannot escape (and staying within 64 meters of them) or (B) by starting the taming process, after which they will never despawn. Asksvin can be tamed by feeding them [[Smoke Puff]]s, [[Vineberry Cluster]]s or [[Fiddlehead]]s. They are rideable by equipping the [[Asksvin Saddle]]. When riding an Asksvin, players cannot attack. Players riding an Asksvin can traverse lava, and neither the player nor Asksvin will take damage from the lava. Tamed Asksvin do not do friendly fire damage to players, any other tamed creatures or neutral [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]]. == Breeding == Asksvin can breed, provided the Asksvin is happy and well-fed with [[Fiddlehead]] or [[Vineberry Cluster]] or [[Smoke Puff]], along with there being another Asksvin within four meters, and no more than 10 Asksvin within at least 10 meters. Once the conditions are met, they will accumulate love points with one another until the pregnancy starts. Pregnancy lasts 60 seconds, checked every 30 seconds, so the egg comes 60 to 90 seconds after it starts. They then lay an [[Asksvin egg]]. The quality of the Asksvin egg is determined by the Asksvin that laid it. A quality 1 egg in the player's inventory indicates a 0-star Asksvin, quality 2 indicates a 1-star, and quality 3 indicates a 2-star. Once laid, it would take 30 minutes to hatch into Asksvin Hatchling if there is a heat source nearby (Example [[Campfire]]). If the heat source is gone or the player puts the egg into their inventory, the timer is reset. Then the Asksvin Hatchling takes 50 minutes to grow into an adult without the need of heat source. They will not breed if the cap is reached, which is 10 Asksvin in 10 meters. However, there is currently no known limit to the eggs themselves. == Trivia == * The word "Asksvin" is Swedish for "ash swine." And like swine, the plural for Asksvin is the same as its singular form. * Due to their green and warty appearance, "Pickle-Dog" has gained popularity as a common moniker for Asksvin within the Twitch-Valheim community. {{Creatures}} [[uk:Попелозавр]] [[ru:Пеплозавр]]

== Usage ==
The '''Shield generator''' dome protects the player and structures within:
* Protects from [[Rain]], prevents players from getting the [[Wet Effect]] and structures from being damaged. (Similar to the [[Shelter Effect]])
* Protects from [[Cinder rain]] in [[Ashlands]], prevents the structure from catching on fire from falling cinder.
* Protects against incoming projectiles such as [[Creatures]] attacks.
* Protects against [[Lava]] balls randomly coming from lava lakes, useful when mining [[Flametal Ore Vein]]s close to lava edge.

== Behavior ==
The Shield generator can be built upon solid ground, [[Cage Structures|Cage]], [[Stone Structures|Stone]], [[Black Marble Structures|Black marble]] or [[Grausten Structures|Grausten]] structures.

The radius of effect is 30 meters in a spherical area centered on the Shield generator.

The generator can hold up to 10 [[Bone Fragments]] or [[Charred Bone]] as fuel and consumes one fuel per 500 damage. Damage will occur when a projectile with an origin outside the radius of effect comes into contact with the shield edge, absorbing the projectile in the process. These absorbed projectiles include the environmental Cinders, and any combat projectiles, ranged or magical, produced by players or creatures. Although the effects of Rain are nullified by the shield, this effect will not cause damage, or consume fuel of the shield generator.

The radius of two or more shields overlapping will result in their intersection combining, allowing multiple shields to be chained together into a larger shield.

== Trivia ==
* Due to the shield determining whether to block an incoming projectile based on its origin position, it is possible for the player to fire a projectile from within the shielded region, and as it exits and re-enters the region, will not be absorbed by the shield.
* Though the effects of Rain are nullified, the Shield generator will not protect [[Fire Effect]] yielding structures from being extinguished, still requiring Shelter.

== Tips ==
* The Shield generator is useful for [[Farming (Skill)|Farming]], where most crops must not be placed under Shelter, normally forcing the player to farm under the effects of rain.
